title: Add tfstate checkpoint shim and zone-aware GPU stride allocator module
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have grown more brittle during mid-rollout upgrades and cross-tenant GPU capacity shuffles. Two recurring failure modes were identified: (1) tfstate drift / partial apply failures leaving resource sets half-created and (2) GPU node fragmentation that increases preemption and reduces packing efficiency across tenants. This PR introduces a small, backward-compatible tfstate checkpoint shim and a new 'gpu-stride-allocator' terraform module to reduce fragmentation and enable safer rollbacks.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a tfstate checkpoint shim that writes periodic, signed checkpoints to the existing state backend namespace. The shim exposes a lightweight CLI invoked by the existing tf-orchestrator: `tfstate-checkpoint create|list|restore`. Checkpoints are indexed by workflow id, timestamp, and a short integrity hash.
- Introduces `modules/gpu-stride-allocator` to allocate GPU node ranges using a configurable stride/stride-offset strategy (zone-aware). The allocator produces an immutable reference map that the nodepool module consumes to create nodepools in contiguous ranges, reducing scattering during tenant scale-ups.
- Adds an apply-wrapper hook `scripts/terraform-apply-safe` that optionally uses the latest checkpoint to do a dry-run restore for failed applies and coordinates a canary step before a full apply.
- IAM: adds templates for role bindings scoped to allocator identities, minimizing wide grants. Templates are backwards-compatible and opt-in by variable.
- Networking: small migration helper to copy VPC route table tags into the new `network/claims` index so upgrades can reconcile route ownership without manual tag edits.

Why this is safe: the shim is additive and opt-in. Existing modules continue to work when the allocator is not enabled. Checkpoint restore requires an explicit CLI invocation or the apply-wrapper opt-in flag. The stride allocator only changes how ranges are computed and does not change instance types or sizes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for checkpoint metadata serialization and restore simulation
- [x] Integration harness run against a 3-zone staging cluster (non-destructive)
- [x] Backwards-compatible IAM templates and docs
- [x] Release notes and operator runbook draft

Usage notes for operators: After merging, teams can enable the allocator by setting `enable_stride_allocator = true` on the tenant profile and providing `stride` and `base_offset` variables. The tfstate-checkpoint CLI must be added to the Managed Apply image if operators want automated checkpoint creation. Documentation is included under `docs/operators/tfstate-checkpoints.md`.

Related: ENG-1953 tracks rollout automation improvements; SUP-4219 contains a customer report that motivated checkpointing.

merge_result:
Merge commit message: Add tfstate checkpoint shim and gpu-stride-allocator module

Squashed commit includes CLI, allocator, IAM templates, network migration helper and docs.
release_notes: Operators: New opt-in features — (1) tfstate checkpoint shim. Add `tfstate-checkpoint` to the managed apply image to enable periodic checkpoints. Use `tfstate-checkpoint restore` to perform staged rollbacks. (2) GPU stride allocator module: opt-in via `enable_stride_allocator = true` in tenant profiles; reduces node fragmentation during tenant scale events. IAM templates are opt-in and scope allocator identities. See docs/operators/tfstate-checkpoints.md for runbook and troubleshooting.
additional_notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing existing state backends or performing automatic restores during cluster upgrades. Checkpoint creation and restore remain operator-controlled. We will follow up with drive-mode telemetry to observe allocator effectiveness before making it the default.
